blocks.text: For more than four months, officials in the southwestern Korean city of Jeongeup held the passport of a seasonal worker from the Philippines. The worker was among 60 foreign nationals whose passports were retained by the city government to prevent them from leaving their assigned workplaces, according to an SBS report Tuesday. Jeongeup, located in North Jeolla Province, participates in a government-run program that brings foreign nationals to Korea for short-term work during peak farming and fishing seasons, when rural communities face labor shortages. City officials initially said the passports were being held under an agreement with the Philippine government. READ: […]...
